- At $P$ on $\omega_1$: $\angle APQ = 30°$ gives inscribed angle $\angle PBA = 30°$.

$$PA = \frac{\sin 15°}{\sin 135°} = \frac{(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})/4}{\sqrt{2}/2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}, \qquad QA = \frac{\sin 30°}{\sin 135°} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.$$

Direction of $PA$: $30°$ from $x$-axis, so:
$$A = \left(\tfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{4},\; \tfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}\right).$$

$$B = \left(\tfrac{1-\sqrt{3}}{4},\; \tfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{4}\right).$$

## Finding $X$ (on $\omega_1$, with $PX \parallel QB$)

Direction of $QB = B - Q = \left(\frac{-(3+\sqrt{3})}{4}, \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{4}\right) \propto (-\sqrt{3}, 1)$, which is angle $150°$.

$$X = \left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}-3}{4},\; \tfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}\right).$$

Note $X_y = A_y = \frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}$, so $AX$ is **horizontal**:
$$AX = \left|\tfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{4} - \tfrac{\sqrt{3}-3}{4}\right| = \tfrac{6-2\sqrt{3}}{4} = \tfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$

## Finding $Y$ (on $\omega_2$, with $QY \parallel PB$)

Direction of $PB = B - P = \left(\frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{4}, \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{4}\right)$. Its slope is $\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{1-\sqrt{3}} = -(2+\sqrt{3}) = \tan 105°$, so $PB$ is at angle $105°$.

$$Y = \left(\tfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{4},\; \tfrac{5+3\sqrt{3}}{4}\right).$$

Note $Y_x = A_x = \frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{4}$, so $AY$ is **vertical**:
$$AY = \tfrac{5+3\sqrt{3}}{4} - \tfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4} = \tfrac{6+2\sqrt{3}}{4} = \tfrac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$

## The Ratio

$$\frac{AX}{AY} = \frac{(3-\sqrt{3})/2}{(3+\sqrt{3})/2} = \frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{3+\sqrt{3}} = \frac{(3-\sqrt{3})^2}{(3+\sqrt{3})(3-\sqrt{3})} = \frac{12 - 6\sqrt{3}}{6} = 2 - \sqrt{3}.$$

$$\boxed{\dfrac{AX}{AY} = 2 - \sqrt{3}}$$
